How to use this notebook:

- Draft by hand, one function per chunk. Run a chunk with Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter).
- Put a check immediately below each function so you see failures while the code is fresh.
- Drafts stay here until they work. The promotion checklist at the end moves one into the package.

## Cholesky decomposition

```{r draft-1}
#' Decorrelate vector by cholesky decomposition
#'
#' I grabbed the definition from here: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitening_transformation#Definition
#' the code: NA handling, recycling, warnings, side effects.
#'
#' @param x matrix of variables to decorrelate
#' @param E variance covariance matrix of vector elements, should be a square matrix
#' @param center default is FALSE, whether the returned matrix should be centered at zero in every dimmension. The default returns a matrix where each dimmension is centered at it's mean
#' @return matrix of decorrelated variables, same shape as x
#' @export
#' @examples
#' # Define mean vector and positive-definite covariance matrix
#' mu <- c(8, 5)
#' E <- matrix(c(2, 1.9, 1.9, 2), nrow = 2)
#' X <- MASS::mvrnorm(n = 100, mu = mu, Sigma = E)
#' cholesky_decorrelate(X, E)
cholesky_decorrelate <- function(x, E, center = F) {
  # Validate: type, length, missing values, empty input.
  stopifnot(is.numeric(x), is.numeric(E), !is.null(x), !is.null(E), !any(is.na(x)), !any(is.na(E)), all(dim(x) > 1), all(dim(E) > 1), all(diag(E) > 0))
  # whitening operations need centered data
  mu <- colMeans(x)
  # invert the matrix
  E_inv <- solve(E)
  # cholesky decomposition
  W = chol(E_inv)
  # transpose decomposed matrix
  # t(W) %*% W %*% E gives the identity matrix
  Wt <- t(W)
  # decorrelation
  y = sweep(x, 2, mu, "-") %*% Wt
  # Return decorrelated values with or without mean
  if(!center){
    return(sweep(y, 2, mu, "+"))  
  } else{
    return(y)
  }
}

# compare correlated and uncorrelated data
plot(X)
points(cholesky_decorrelate(X, E, center = F), pch = 16)

mu <- c(8, 5)
E <- matrix(c(1, 0, 0, 1), nrow = 2)
X <- mvrnorm(n = 100, mu = mu, Sigma = E)

plot(X)
points(cholesky_decorrelate(X, E, center = F), pch = 16)
```

```{r draft-1-checks, eval=FALSE}
# Happy path: exact expected values, not just "it ran".
# identity matrix does does nothing
stopifnot(all( (cholesky_decorrelate(X, E) - X) < 1e-16))
# input and output dimmensions match
stopifnot(all(dim(X) == dim(cholesky_decorrelate(X, E))))

# Edges worth covering for almost any function:
# - empty input:        draft_fn(numeric(0))
# - missing values:     draft_fn(c(1, NA, 3))
# - wrong type:         testthat::expect_error(draft_fn("x"), "numeric")
# - length one:         draft_fn(1)
# - degenerate stats:   draft_fn(rep(5, 10))  # zero variance
```


## Promote to the package

1. Move the function into the matching module in `R/`: `plotting.R`, `file_management.R`, `statistics.R`, or `popgen.R`.
2. Complete the roxygen block, then run `devtools::document()`.
3. Add tests to `tests/testthat/test-<module>.R`, then run `devtools::test(filter = "<module>")`.
4. Run the full suite with `devtools::test()`.
5. Bump `Version:` in `DESCRIPTION`: `feat:` minor, `fix:` patch, breaking major.
6. Commit with a semantic prefix (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `test:`, `docs:`, `chore:`).

## Before you call it done

- [ ] Every argument is documented and validated.
- [ ] The return value has one predictable shape.
- [ ] Empty, `NA`, and wrong-type inputs behave as documented.
- [ ] At least one test asserts exact values, not just absence of errors.
- [ ] `devtools::check()` (or `R CMD build` + `R CMD check`) is clean for this change.
